Definition: from G303 and the middle voice of G5021; to arrange:--set in order.
BiblicalUsage: The word appears once, in the first verse of Luke's gospel: 'Forasmuch as many have taken in hand to set forth in order a declaration of those things which are most surely believed among us.' It is the arranging, the setting in order — Luke taking the accounts others had written and putting them in order, so Theophilus could know the certainty of what he had been taught.
TheologicalSignificance: One word for setting in order carries no doctrine of its own; its weight is the gospel itself — Luke arranging the story so that certainty could follow.
